png-to-pdf.quickAnswer: Add your PNG files, put them in order with the up/down controls, pick a page size (Fit to image, A4, or Letter), and build a real PDF document where every image sits centered on its own page — no upload, no watermark.
keyFacts: Each PNG becomes one full PDF page, in the exact order shown in the queue.
"Fit to image" makes every page exactly the size of its image — perfect for screenshots.
A4 and Letter modes center each image with an adjustable margin (0–40 mm).
Images are embedded losslessly — PNG pixels are stored without recompression.
Up to 10 MB per image; add as many images as your device memory allows.
howTo: Add one or more PNG files (each up to 10 MB).
Reorder pages with the up/down arrows, or remove images you do not need.
Choose page size: Fit to image, A4, or Letter, plus orientation and margin.
Click "Build PDF" and review the output size shown on the download button.
png-to-pdf.formula:
page_width_pt = image_width_px × (72 / 96)
scale_to_fit = min(avail_w / img_w, avail_h / img_h)

Browsers treat images at 96 DPI, while a PDF point is 1/72 inch — so a 1920 px wide screenshot is 1440 pt wide on a Fit page. In A4/Letter mode the image is scaled to the largest size that fits inside the margins, keeping its aspect ratio.
png-to-pdf.workedExample: Three phone screenshots (1170 × 2532 px each) with "Fit to image" produce a 3-page PDF where each page is exactly 877.5 × 1899 pt. Switch to A4 portrait with 10 mm margins and each screenshot is centered at about 539 × 1166 pt on a standard A4 sheet — ready to print or email.
benefits: True PDF output — a real document structure, not a renamed image file.
Visual page queue with numbered badges makes ordering mistakes obvious.
Fit/A4/Letter covers screenshots, documents, and print in one place.
Runs fully offline after load; no account or upload needed.
limitations: Only PNG images are accepted — convert JPGs with the JPG to PDF tool.
Output pages are image-only; text inside images is not selectable or searchable.
Very large image sets can exhaust mobile browser memory.
No OCR: scanned text stays as pictures of text.
png-to-pdf.privacyNote: Your images are assembled into a PDF entirely on your device using pdf-lib. No file is uploaded, and nothing is retained after you close the page.

faqs.q: Will my PNG lose quality in the PDF?
faqs.a: No. PNG data is embedded without recompression, so pixels are preserved exactly. The only change is the page-size math that positions the image.
It makes each PDF page exactly the pixel dimensions of its image (at 96 DPI), so a screenshot fills its page edge to edge with no white borders.
Use the up and down arrow buttons on each queue item. The numbered badges always show the final page order.

faqs.q: Can I mix portrait and landscape images?
faqs.a: Yes. In Fit mode each page matches its own image. In A4/Letter mode choose one orientation and every image is centered on that sheet.

faqs.q: Why is my PDF bigger than the PNGs?
faqs.a: PDF adds document structure around the images. With lossless PNG embedding the overhead is small — usually a few kilobytes per page.

faqs.q: Can I add a JPG too?
faqs.a: This tool accepts PNG only, to keep its behavior predictable. Use the JPG to PDF tool for JPEG images.
